MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-02-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Meeting ID: ff-20250218-ATLAS-POC-001
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Nora Singh (Redwood Solutions), Priya Raman (CTO, AtlasHealth), Ben Carter (Platform Lead), Liam O'Neill (Security Engineer)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto gen, may be imperfect):
- Purpose: scope a private-network POC (VPC peering / PrivateLink) to validate regional data residency and performance for AtlasHealth production workloads.
- Success criteria discussed: p95 inference latency targets, throughput baseline, no data egress outside approved regions, and audit/keys in customer control.
- Next steps: share network checklist and benchmark plan; confirm regions and CIDRs; schedule hands-on validation.

TOPICS COVERED:
- VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink tradeoffs
- Region residency (us-east-1 vs eu-west-1) and cross-border egress constraints
- Egress/NAT/IP address exposure and audit logging (CloudTrail, flow logs)
- KMS/HSM key control and envelope encryption; rotation policies
- Benchmarking plan: sample request patterns, p95 targets, token throughput, cold vs warm cache tests
- POC timeline and decision gates

ACTION ITEMS (summarized inside transcript): see metadata action_items above for structured items.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros and then we'll dive into the private networking scoping.
[00:14] Priya (AtlasHealth): Hi, I'm Priya, CTO at AtlasHealth. We're trying to run PHI-adjacent inferencing for triage workflows but need to ensure data never leaves the EU and we want network isolation.
[00:27] Ben (AtlasHealth): Ben here, I own the platform side, I'll be doing the AWS setup with our infra team.
[00:33] Liam (AtlasHealth): Liam, security — mostly focused on key management, audit logs, and egress controls.
[00:38] Marcus (Redwood): Marcus from Redwood, I'll own the bench marking and performance side for the POC.
[00:42] Nora (Redwood): Nora — solutions, I'll help with the network setup & docs.
[00:46] Avery: Great. So high level we want to scope a 4-week-ish POC where we validate two things: 1) that we can keep inference traffic inside eu-west-1 (for example) via PrivateLink or VPC peering and 2) that performance meets your p95 latency SLAs.
[01:07] Priya: Right, and we also need to prove that the model inputs and logs won't ever be replicated to a non-EU region. We have customer legal saying data at rest and in transit must remain in region.
[01:21] Avery: Understood. Two immediate network patterns we typically propose: classic VPC peering (cross-account) or AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). There are pros/cons — peering is lower-latency but requires route table controls; PrivateLink gives you more control over egress because traffic terminates on an ENI in your VPC.
[01:44] Ben: Also curious about IP egress — if we peer, will the outbound IPs be our CIDR or Redwood's IP? That matters for firewall rules.
[01:52] Marcus: Good question — with VPC peering traffic stays in the AWS backbone and uses your source IPs; with PrivateLink the traffic goes to a service endpoint with its own ENI, so outbound IP might appear as Redwood-managed ENI unless you use NAT in your VPC. There's nuance and we'll document exact behavior per cloud provider.
[02:11] Liam: We need to ensure we can produce audited evidence that nothing was routed through a US region. CloudTrail + VPC flow logs should be in place, also want to know where logs live.
[02:20] Nora: For Private deployments (Redwood Private) the control plane can be customer-managed so logs and KMS can be anchored to your account. For hosted options we provide assurances but data may flow to Redwood-managed infrastructure in-region unless PrivateLink/peering is used.
[02:39] Priya: Let me clarify — we want the control plane in eu-west-1 too, ideally customer-managed, or at least the data plane pinned to eu-west-1. Is that doable?
[02:50] Avery: Yes, for Private deployments or Dedicated pools we can pin model execution to a region and in many cases can run with a customer VPC peered to our compute VPC in the same region so data doesn't leave the region. The control plane for managed services sometimes remains centralized; we can offer a private control plane option. We'll flag that as a requirement.
[03:09] Ben: Regarding network setup, what's the typical ticket of work on our side? Route tables, endpoints, IAM role for the peering, maybe Service Consumer/Provider setup for PrivateLink?
[03:21] Nora: Exactly — the checklist we'll share covers: VPC IDs and CIDRs, account IDs, desired subnets for endpoints, security group rules (ports), route table modifications, and optional NAT/GW decisions if PrivateLink used. We also include IAM role steps for cross-account roles if required.
[03:36] Marcus: On benchmarking — we need to agree a workload. For triage workflows we usually see short inputs (~100 tokens) with bursts at peak and sustained low-rate. For success criteria can we target p95 <= 200ms for single-shot generation on a 2k context model? Also throughput target say 200 reqs/s?
[03:58] Priya: Our legal ops said 150ms p95 is preferable for UI latency. Is 150 realistic?
[04:06] Marcus: 150 is aggressive depending on model size and quantization. On dedicated GPU with optimized batching we can aim for 150-200ms p95 for shorter contexts. For reference we'll run cold-start and warm-cache tests; warm cache should be significantly lower latency. We should also measure end-to-end (including network hop) which will be included in the POC.
[04:28] Avery: We'll propose baseline targets: p95 <= 200ms (primary), p95 <= 150ms (stretch). Throughput baseline we can tune with batching and continuous KV cache. We'll include model variants (quantized vs fp16) to find cost vs latency sweet spot.
[04:44] Ben: Cost is important — can you give rough per-million-token price differences between hosted vs dedicated private deployments?
[04:52] Avery: We can provide estimates in the pricing deck but rough rule: dedicated/private is higher base monthly but lower per-token over scale; hosted is lowest operational friction but higher per-token. For the POC we'll include an apples-to-apples cost model using your expected token volumes.
[05:06] Liam: For encryption and keys — we must be able to use our KMS keys, preferably a customer-managed CMK with rotation policy. Any objections?
[05:14] Nora: No, that's supported for private deployments. For some hosted integrations we can support customer-managed keys via a cross-account grant, but the safest is Private control plane where the keys never leave your account. We'll document exact patterns.
[05:28] Priya: What about egress charges if we use PrivateLink vs peering? We have a concern about the NAT gateway charges and inter-AZ traffic.
[05:36] Marcus: PrivateLink has per-GB charges on AWS plus per-hour endpoint hourly costs; peering doesn't have the endpoint cost but may cause cross-AZ or cross-account charges depending on setup. We'll calculate rough egress cost for the benchmark traffic in the plan.
[05:52] Ben: How do we validate that logs don't contain raw customer data? We need redaction or retention windows.
[05:58] Avery: Good point — Redwood has options for token-level redaction and we can set retention windows for request logs. For the POC we'll demonstrate log configuration where full request bodies are either never written to long-term storage or are stored encrypted with your CMK and short TTL.
[06:13] Priya: For acceptance criteria, my list is: 1) traffic never leaves eu-west-1, 2) p95 latency meets target, 3) audit logs available and under our KMS, 4) cost within agreed threshold. Anything missing?
[06:27] Marcus: Also include reliability — sustained 99.9% successful request rate during benchmark windows, and a fallback plan for model variant if capacity constrained.
[06:36] Liam: I'd add we need an architecture diagram and a one-page security control list showing where each control maps to SOC2/ISO categories.
[06:43] Avery: We'll include that as part of the artifacts.
[06:47] Priya: Timeline — can you lay out a week-by-week plan?
[06:52] Marcus: Proposed POC timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope and get account/region info, share network checklist
- Week 1: network setup (peering or PrivateLink), IAM roles, certificate/KMS prep, basic smoke tests
- Week 2: deploy models, run baseline benchmarks (cold starts, warm cache), measure p95 and throughput
- Week 3: tuning (batching, quantization, autoscaling), re-run benchmarks, cost analysis
- Week 4: final evaluation, run audit log extraction, decision meeting with execs.
[07:34] Priya: That aligns with our timelines; legal will need 2-3 days to review any data processing addendum but we can run the network setup in parallel.
[07:44] Ben: On the network side we prefer PrivateLink if it reduces our operational route table complexity, but we need the traffic source ip to be our own — does PrivateLink break that?
[07:54] Nora: PrivateLink uses service ENIs; the service endpoint's source IP is the ENI's IP, so outbound IP may not be in your CIDR. You can NAT from your subnet to preserve egress IPs, or we can set up a transit pattern but that adds complexity. We'll map options in the doc.
[08:10] Marcus: Also for measuring end-to-end we will have a lightweight agent or lambda in your VPC that calls the Redwood endpoint and measures the full RTT to include network overhead.
[08:20] Priya: For models — can you run our private finetuned weights or do we need to use Redwood-curated models?
[08:28] Avery: Both are possible. For hosted we often run curated models; for private/dedicated we can load customer models as long as licensing and packaging is sane. We'll need to exchange model artifacts securely — S3 presigned objects with limited TTL or a secure transfer method.
[08:44] Liam: Any concerns about side-channel logs or metadata? We need assurance that no prompts are written to cheap analytics buckets in a way that is queryable.
[08:53] Marcus: We'll demonstrate the log pipeline configuration during the POC — show that request/response bodies are either never forwarded to analytics or are encrypted with your CMK and have tight TTLs.
[09:02] Priya: Great. Anything else on the technical constraints?
[09:06] Ben: For the peering approach if we do cross-account we have to ensure route table propagation and avoid overlapping CIDRs; we'll provide a list of non-overlapping ranges.
[09:16] Nora: Also worth noting if AtlasHealth requires on-prem connectivity, we can discuss Direct Connect / VPN patterns but that's out of scope for first pass.
[09:26] Avery: Okay to recap: we'll send the network checklist, PrivateLink vs peering doc, IAM snippets, and a benchmark plan. Marcus will own the bench plan and run the initial tests. AtlasHealth will confirm EU region and CIDRs. We target starting network setup next week.
[09:46] Priya: Sounds good. One more ask — can we get a sample compliance evidence pack? Even a skeleton of SOC2 artifacts you can share?
[09:56] Avery: Yes, we'll include a redacted SOC2 summary and a list of available artifacts and the process to request them under NDA.
[10:04] Liam: I'll need that to share with our auditors.
[10:08] Avery: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the network validation call. Thanks everyone.
[10:13] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.

END TRANSCRIPT
